sections.content:
Population change in Broxtowe in 2032

The population in Broxtowe is projected to increase from 112,395 people in 2022 to 118,005 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 4,691 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Broxtowe
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Broxtowe, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 2,748, with 9,906 births and 12,654 deaths in Broxtowe between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Broxtowe by 2.4%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 4,040, with 101,510 people moving to the area and 97,470 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Broxtowe by 3.6%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 335, with 1,690 people moving to the area and 2,025 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Broxtowe by 0.3%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 4,691, with 9,819 people moving to the area and 5,128 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Broxtowe by 4.2%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Broxtowe in 2032

The median age in Broxtowe is projected to remain the same at 42 years between 2022 and 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 22% of the population in Broxtowe are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 21% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Broxtowe between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Broxtowe is projected to stay the same, at around 64%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to fall from 330 to 325 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Broxtowe?

In 2032, 17% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 20% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Broxtowe between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 6%
